correctness.rationale: For fixed zero sets of sizes p,q, a positive A vertex at a common-positive index can cover all q B zeros for excess ceil(q/2) above one. If no common-positive defender is used, each A defender misses its own opposite zero, so at least two are necessary and two distinct ones suffice at cost 2ceil((q-1)/2), if available. The same argument holds on B, independently, with zero cost when there are no zeros to defend. This gives the exact support formula and the bound w>=2n-floor(p/2)-floor(q/2). If an entire shore is zero, the other cannot have any zeros and the cost is at least n+2ceil((n-1)/2), strictly above the matched-pair witness for n>=3. For n=2m+1, equality forces both zero counts 2m (the floor drops at 2m-1), and the only positives must form a deleted matched pair. For n=2m, equality forces p,q in {n-2,n-1}; only a common-positive defender can realize equality if n>=6 because the two-defender excess is strictly larger. At n=4 a side with two opposite zeros also has strict excess for inside-only defense. For three opposite zeros the possible cost tie cannot occur at equality: the opposite shore has a sole positive which must have a common-positive index; this leaves at most one inside-index candidate. With nonempty support intersection exactly the five claimed support patterns remain, and on each side only one common-positive vertex carries excess. The counts are n; n(n-1) each for the asymmetric 2-by-1 cases; n(n-1)(n-2) for two 2-supports meeting once; and 4 binom(n,2) for identical 2-supports. Summing gives n(n^2+n-1) for even n. The labels fit the degree-based cap and each listed family attains the lower bound.
residual_risks: The bounded runs are corroboration; completeness for unbounded n is from the exact support argument.
